Kauṭalya
a form of the name of the a. of Arthaśāstra; variant noted in the Mysore edn.; an. the only form known to the Paṭṭan ms. See T. Ganapati Sastri, p. 4, Eng. Intro. to his TSS. edn. of Arthaśāstra Vol. I, on Kauṭalya a. the correct form derived from Kuṭala, a gotra-name. But see contra, P. V. Kane, HDS. I. p.. 90-1, according to whom Kuṭala a. gotra-name is [Page101-a. known only from later texts an. nibandhas.
See also J. Jolly, ‘Kauṭilya oder Kauṭalya ?’ ZII. V. (1927), p.. 216-221. H. Berger, ‘Kauṭalya ist alter als Kauṭilya’, Munchener Studien zur Sprachwissenschaft, Heft 6, Munich, 1955, p.. 27-29. T. Burrow, ‘Cāṇakya an. Kauṭalya’, ABORI. Golden Jubilee Vol. 1968, p.. 24-28.

Kauṭilya
known also by the names Cāṇakya an. Viṣṇugupta; reputed a. a. of the Arthaśāstra, known after him a. Kauṭa(ṭi)līya.
--Arthaśāstra.
See NCC. I. Revised edn. p. 387 ff. under Arthaśāstra.
In the concluding verse of the Arthaśāstra, the work is said to comprise Sūtras an. Bhāṣya (cakāra sūtram ca bhāṣyam ca).
For points of textual criticism bearing on this text see under Artha śāstra in NCC. I. Revised edn. p. 388b.
See also below Cāṇakya where works going under that name in Nīti, Jyotiṣa an. med. are noted.
